title: Building Images & Managing Environment Variables 🏗️
description: Integrate Dockerfiles into Compose and use environment variables and .env files effectively.

slides.title: Building Images with Compose 🏗️
slides.content:
# `build` vs `image`

You can have Compose build your image from a Dockerfile:
```yaml
services:
  app:
    build:
      context: ./app       # path to Dockerfile directory
      dockerfile: Dockerfile.dev  # optional, default is 'Dockerfile'
      args:                # build args
        - NODE_ENV=development
```

Then `docker compose build` builds all services with `build` defined. `docker compose up --build` forces a rebuild before starting.

> If you also specify `image`, Compose tags the built image with that name.

slides.title: Build Example 🔨
slides.codeSnippet:
services:
  frontend:
    build:
      context: ./frontend
      args:
        API_URL: http://backend:3000
    ports:
      - "80:80"
  backend:
    build: ./backend
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"

quizData.question: How do you force Docker Compose to rebuild images before starting services?
quizData.explanation: `docker compose up --build` will build images (if build context defined) before starting containers.

slides.title: Environment Variables in Compose 🌍
slides.content:
# Injecting Configuration

You can define environment variables directly in the compose file:
```yaml
environment:
  - NODE_ENV=production
  - API_KEY=12345
```

Or use an `.env` file (placed next to compose.yaml):
```
# .env
NODE_ENV=development
API_KEY=dev_key
```

In compose.yaml, reference them with `${VARIABLE}`:
```yaml
environment:
  - NODE_ENV=${NODE_ENV}
```

> Compose automatically reads the `.env` file in the project directory. You can specify a different file with `--env-file`.

slides.title: Secrets vs Environment Variables 🤫
slides.content:
# For Sensitive Data

Never put secrets directly in `compose.yaml` or `.env` if committed to version control. Use:
- **Compose secrets** (Swarm only)
- Runtime injection via `env_file` with a file outside VCS
- Docker secrets (Swarm)

For local development, you can use an `override` file (`compose.override.yaml`) that is gitignored.

quizData.question: If you have a `.env` file with `APP_PORT=5000`, how can you use it in `compose.yaml`?

options.text: It's automatically available in all containers

quizData.explanation: Compose substitutes `${VAR}` with the value from the `.env` file (or the host's environment if set).

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Override Files
`compose.override.yaml` is automatically merged on top of `compose.yaml` (when both exist). Use it for development‑specific settings (bind mounts, debug ports).
